prophecies.title: The Woman's Offspring
prophecies.explanation: The first messianic prophecy in the Bible. God promises that the woman's offspring will crush the serpent's head, even though the serpent will strike his heel. This points forward to Jesus' victory over Satan through the cross.

prophecies.title: Abraham's Offspring
prophecies.explanation: God promised Abraham that all families of the earth would be blessed through his offspring. Paul explains that this refers to Christ, the one offspring who was to bring blessing to all nations.

prophecies.title: From the Tribe of Judah
prophecies.explanation: Jacob prophesied that the scepter would not depart from Judah until the Prince of Peace comes. Jesus was descended from Judah and is called 'the Lion of the tribe of Judah'.

prophecies.title: David's Descendant
prophecies.explanation: God promised David that his descendant would build a house for God's name and that his royal throne would be established forever. Jesus is the 'Son of David' who inherits the eternal kingdom.

prophecies.title: The Virgin Birth
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that a virgin would conceive and give birth to a son who would be called Immanuel ('God with us'). Matthew quotes this directly as fulfilled in Jesus' birth.

prophecies.title: Born in Bethlehem
prophecies.explanation: Micah prophesied that Israel's ruler would come from Bethlehem, David's city. When the wise men asked Herod where the Messiah was to be born, the scribes quoted this prophecy.

prophecies.title: Called Out of Egypt
prophecies.explanation: Hosea writes about God's love for Israel: 'Out of Egypt I called my son.' Matthew sees this fulfilled when Joseph took Jesus and Mary to Egypt to flee from Herod, and later returned.

prophecies.title: The Massacre in Bethlehem
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah describes Rachel weeping for her children in Ramah. Matthew sees this fulfilled in Herod's brutal murder of the boys in Bethlehem as he tried to kill Jesus.

prophecies.title: The Forerunner in the Wilderness
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied about a voice crying out in the wilderness, preparing the way for the Lord. John the Baptist identified himself with this prophecy and called the people to repentance before the Messiah came.

prophecies.title: Elijah Must Come
prophecies.explanation: Malachi prophesied that Elijah would come before the great day of the Lord. Jesus declared that John the Baptist was the fulfillment of this prophecy, as he came in the spirit and power of Elijah.

prophecies.title: Light over Galilee
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that a great light would shine over Galilee, the land of the Gentiles. Jesus began his public ministry right in Galilee, and Matthew sees this as the fulfillment of the prophecy.

prophecies.title: Anointing of the Spirit
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that the Lord's Spirit would rest upon the shoot from Jesse's root. At Jesus' baptism, the Spirit came down like a dove, and Jesus later declared in the synagogue at Nazareth that this prophecy was fulfilled.

prophecies.title: Healing of the blind and deaf
prophecies.explanation: The prophet Isaiah foretold that when God comes, the blind will see, the deaf will hear, and the lame will leap. When John the Baptist sent a message to Jesus, he pointed specifically to these signs as proof that he was the Messiah.

prophecies.title: A Speech in Parables
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist wrote that he would open his mouth with parables and proclaim riddles from ancient times. Matthew sees this fulfilled in Jesus' extensive use of parables in his teaching.

prophecies.title: A Prophet Like Moses
prophecies.explanation: Moses promised that God would raise up a prophet like himself, and the people must listen to him. Peter and Stephen in the Acts of the Apostles identify Jesus as this prophet.

prophecies.title: Entry on a Donkey
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah prophesied that the King of Zion would come riding on a donkey, humble and righteous. On Palm Sunday, Jesus entered Jerusalem riding on a donkey while the people shouted 'Hosanna'.

prophecies.title: Zeal for God's house
prophecies.explanation: David wrote about zeal for God's house that consumes him. When Jesus cleansed the temple and drove out the money changers, the disciples remembered this psalm.

prophecies.title: The cornerstone that was rejected
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist wrote that the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. Jesus applied this to himself after the parable of the vineyard, and Peter confirms that this is fulfilled in Christ.

prophecies.title: Betrayed by a friend
prophecies.explanation: David lamented that his close friend, who ate at his table, had lifted his heel against him. Jesus quoted this regarding Judas Iscariot before he was betrayed.

prophecies.title: Sold for Thirty Pieces of Silver
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah described how the shepherd was valued at thirty silver pieces, the price of a slave, which were thrown to the potter in the temple. Judas received exactly this amount for betraying Jesus.

prophecies.title: The Shepherd Struck, the Sheep Scattered
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah prophesied that when the shepherd is struck, the sheep will be scattered. Jesus quoted this to his disciples before his arrest and predicted they would all abandon him.

prophecies.title: False Witnesses
prophecies.explanation: David complained that false witnesses rose up against him. At Jesus' trial, the council tried to find false witnesses to condemn him.

prophecies.title: Silent Before His Accusers
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that the Lord's servant would not open his mouth, like a lamb led to slaughter. Jesus remained silent during the accusations from the chief priests and Pilate's interrogation.

prophecies.title: Spit Upon and Beaten
prophecies.explanation: The Lord's servant in Isaiah offered his back to those who struck him, and did not hide his face from shame and spitting. Jesus was spat upon and beaten by both the council and the Roman soldiers.

prophecies.title: Hated Without Cause
prophecies.explanation: David wrote that those who hate him without cause are more than the hairs of his head. Jesus said that the world hated him without cause, and that this fulfilled Scripture.

prophecies.title: The Crucifixion
prophecies.explanation: David described hands and feet being pierced—a remarkable prophecy written centuries before crucifixion was used as an execution method. Jesus died by crucifixion.

prophecies.title: Numbered with Transgressors
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that the Lord’s servant would be numbered among transgressors. Jesus was crucified between two criminals and quoted this prophecy himself before his arrest.

prophecies.title: Mocked on the Cross
prophecies.explanation: David described how those who saw him mocked him, sneered and shook their heads, saying he should let the Lord rescue him. The passersby at the cross taunted Jesus with almost identical words.

prophecies.title: Garments divided by casting lots
prophecies.explanation: David prophesied that they would divide his garments among them and cast lots for his robe. At the crucifixion, the soldiers divided Jesus' clothes and cast lots for his tunic, just as predicted.

prophecies.title: Gall and vinegar
prophecies.explanation: David wrote that they gave him gall to eat and vinegar to drink. At the crucifixion, Jesus was offered wine mixed with gall, and later sour wine on a sponge.

prophecies.title: Forsaken by God
prophecies.explanation: Psalm 22 opens with the cry: 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' Jesus cried out these very words from the cross, thereby pointing to this entire messianic psalm.

prophecies.title: No Bone Broken
prophecies.explanation: The psalmist wrote that the Lord guards all his bones; not one of them shall be broken. The soldiers broke the legs of the two thieves, but Jesus was already dead, so his legs were not broken - also in accordance with the regulations for the Passover lamb.

prophecies.title: Pierced
prophecies.explanation: Zechariah prophesied that they will look on him whom they have pierced and mourn for him. A soldier thrust a spear into Jesus' side, and John quotes this as the fulfillment of the prophecy.

prophecies.title: The Suffering Servant
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah 53 describes the Lord's suffering servant who bore our sicknesses and was wounded for our transgressions. This is one of the clearest prophetic pictures of Jesus' substitutionary suffering and death.

prophecies.title: Buried with a rich man
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that the Lord's servant would be buried with a rich man, even though he died among criminals. Joseph of Arimathea, a wealthy man, laid Jesus in his own new tomb.

prophecies.title: The resurrection
prophecies.explanation: David wrote that God would not let His holy one see decay. Peter explained on the day of Pentecost that David could not have written this about himself, for he died and his tomb is still here—but Jesus rose before his body saw decay.

prophecies.title: Rising on the third day
prophecies.explanation: Hosea wrote that God would make us alive after two days and raise us up on the third. Jesus rose from the dead on the third day, just as he himself had predicted.

prophecies.title: The Ascension
prophecies.explanation: David sang that the Lord ascended on high, took captives captive, and gave gifts to men. Paul applies this to Christ's ascension and the distribution of the Spirit's gifts.

prophecies.title: Seated at God's Right Hand
prophecies.explanation: David wrote that the Lord said to my Lord, 'Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.' This is the most quoted psalm in the New Testament and shows the exaltation of the Messiah.

prophecies.title: Priest Forever After the Order of Melchizedek
prophecies.explanation: David prophesied about a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek—one who was both king and priest. The book of Hebrews explains in detail how Jesus fulfills this as our eternal high priest.

prophecies.title: The New Covenant
prophecies.explanation: Jeremiah prophesied that God would establish a new covenant, not like the one He made with their ancestors, but with His law written on their hearts. Jesus instituted this new covenant with His blood at the Last Supper.

prophecies.title: The Outpouring of the Spirit
prophecies.explanation: Joel prophesied that in the last days God would pour out His Spirit on all people, and sons and daughters would prophesy. On the day of Pentecost, Peter declared that this was fulfilled when the Holy Spirit came.

prophecies.title: The Gentiles Included
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that the Lord's servant would be a light for the Gentiles and bring salvation to the ends of the earth. Simeon prophesied this over the child Jesus, and Paul quoted it as the basis for mission to the Gentiles.

prophecies.title: The Destruction of the Temple
prophecies.explanation: Daniel prophesied that after the Anointed One (Messiah) was removed, the city and the sanctuary would be destroyed. Jesus predicted the destruction of the temple, which occurred in AD 70 when the Romans burned Jerusalem.

prophecies.title: The Fall of Babylon
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, would become like Sodom and Gomorrah - never to be inhabited again. Historical Babylon fell to the Persians in 539 BC and gradually decayed into ruins. Revelation uses Babylon as a symbol for the world's evil systems.

prophecies.title: The Destruction of Tyre
prophecies.explanation: Ezekiel prophesied that Tyre would be destroyed by many nations, that its walls would be torn down and its stones cast into the sea. Nebuchadnezzar besieged the city for 13 years, and Alexander the Great completed the destruction by building a causeway from the ruins to reach the island city.

prophecies.title: The Four World Empires
prophecies.explanation: Daniel interpreted Nebuchadnezzar's dream about four world empires: Babylon (gold), Medo-Persia (silver), Greece (bronze), and Rome (iron). History confirmed this sequence, and the prophecy ends with God's eternal kingdom shattering all others.

prophecies.title: The Messiah's Return
prophecies.explanation: Daniel saw one like a son of man coming on the clouds of heaven and receiving eternal dominion. Jesus used this title for himself and prophesied that the Son of Man will come on the clouds of heaven with great power and glory.

prophecies.title: The Day of Judgment
prophecies.explanation: Malachi prophesied about the Lord's great and terrible day that burns like an oven. The New Testament confirms that Jesus will return to judge the living and the dead, and that this world will perish in fire.

prophecies.title: New Heaven and New Earth
prophecies.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that God would create a new heaven and a new earth, where the former things will not be remembered. Revelation ends the Bible with the vision of the new creation where God dwells with his people.

prophecies.title: The Resurrection of the Dead
prophecies.explanation: Daniel prophesied that many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake—some to eternal life, others to eternal contempt. Jesus confirmed this double resurrection, and Revelation describes the final judgment.
